question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in execute-on-parse tool execution mode to agent-core, and should early execution require new tool concurrency-safety metadata first?
rationale: The source-level latency gap is clear, but the fix changes core runtime semantics and safety policy rather than repairing a narrowly broken existing contract.

options.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
options.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner design for streaming scheduling, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and regression proof.

options.title: Wait For Tool Safety Metadata
options.body: Treat early execution as blocked until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62962 or an equivalent concurrency-safety contract exists.

options.title: Defer Runtime Semantics Change
options.body: Keep current post-stream parallel batching as the only supported behavior if maintainers decide early execution is too risky for now.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner design for streaming scheduling, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sits in the current agent-core package and provider stream surfaces where recent history gives the strongest routing signal.
